scenes.visual: close-up illustration of an Indian man's hand holding a plain blue bank card with no markings just above a small black card payment machine with a blank screen on a wooden shop counter, the card tilted toward the machine, the hand and machine in the lower two-thirds of the frame, simple warm shop background
scenes.narration: Ever tapped your card to pay and wondered where the *power* comes from?

scenes.visual: illustration of a small black card payment machine with a blank screen standing alone on a wooden shop counter, a plain blue bank card with no markings lying flat beside it, seen from a slight angle, simple uncluttered background, the objects in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Yesterday's answer: B, the machine. But through thin *air*? And how does the card reply?
scenes.headline: THROUGH *AIR*?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: a dashed card outline; a battery icon gets a red cross, then a thin coil of wire draws itself round the card's edge and the chip appears
scenes.narration: Okay, so look inside a card. No battery. Just a tiny chip... and a thin *wire* coiled round the edge. Why a coil?
scenes.headline: NO *BATTERY*

scenes.visual: illustration of a hand holding a colourful paper pinwheel on a stick in front of a small white table fan, the pinwheel spinning with soft curved motion lines, side view, plain cream background, the fan and pinwheel in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Here's the trick. Hold a paper *pinwheel* far from a fan. Nothing. Bring it close, and it spins.
scenes.headline: LIKE A *PINWHEEL*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the card machine sends out pulsing field rings; a card glides down towards it while a big counter falls from 20 to 2 cm, the coil glows and the chip wakes up
scenes.narration: The machine is that fan. It sends out an invisible magnetic *field*. Bring the card within a few centimetres, and its coil catches enough to wake the chip.
scenes.headline: THE MACHINE'S *FIELD*

scenes.visual: illustration of a hand pressing a plain blue bank card with no markings flat against the top of a small black card payment machine on a wooden shop counter, seen from the side, simple warm background, the hand and machine in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: That's why it's a *tap*, not a wave. But the card has no radio. So how does it *answer*?
scenes.headline: BUT HOW DOES IT *TALK*?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: card resting on the machine; the chip takes more, then less power in a pattern, the field rings pulse bright and dim and the machine's screen fills with ones and zeros
scenes.narration: See, it doesn't send anything out. The chip takes a bit more power, then a bit less, in a *pattern*.
scenes.headline: MORE... *LESS*...

scenes.visual: illustration of a small black card payment machine on a wooden shop counter with a big green tick shape on its screen, a hand lifting a plain blue bank card with no markings away from it, simple warm background, the machine and hand in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: The machine feels those tiny tugs, and reads them as your card. <short pause> So every tap? The machine's doing *all* the work.
scenes.headline: IT *FEELS* THE TUGS

scenes.narration: These legends got it first. Nicely done.
scenes.narration_none: Nobody cracked yesterday's one... <chuckles> let's see if you can beat today's.
scenes.headline: *SHOUTOUT*

scenes.narration: Tomorrow, the two flush buttons. Myth or fact: the small one's the same water, just softer? Comment your guess.

youtube.description:
How does tap to pay work when the card has no battery? Inside a contactless card there's just a tiny chip and a thin coil of wire round the edge. The card machine sends out an invisible magnetic field. Bring the card within a few centimetres and the coil catches enough of it to wake the chip, like a paper pinwheel that only spins close to a fan. The card has no radio of its own, so it answers by taking a bit more power, then a bit less, in a pattern. The machine feels those tiny tugs and reads them as your card.
